study type: In vitro study with case observation
cohort: Isolated primary human cytotrophoblasts were used for in vitro experiments, and term placentas from two patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) receiving Vedolizumab were compared to those of untreated healthy controls.
finding: The study revealed a previously unrecognized role for α4β7 and MAdCAM-1 in human placentation, showing that Vedolizumab and anti-integrin β7 significantly reduced cytotrophoblast invasion and adhesion in vitro, and placentas from Vedolizumab-treated patients exhibited pronounced pathologic features.
